tweets.text: https://t.co/9JFKOz3lEv

augmenting human intellect

when i started making software, i wasn’t dreaming of a factory.

i loved that something on a screen could become an extension of my mind. a place to put a thought before i understood it. to move things around until new connections appeared. to make little systems that worked the way i worked, even if it made no sense to anyone else.

the computer wasn’t interesting because it could do work without me. it was interesting because of what i could do with it.

the early lineage of computing was built around this possibility. in 1962, Engelbart described augmenting human intellect as helping a person understand complex situations and find solutions that were previously out of reach. his starting point was the human being, not the autonomous machine.

he wasn’t describing a faster black box. he was looking at the whole relationship between a person, their tools, their language, their methods, and what they could learn to do with them. the capability belonged to that whole system.

somewhere along the way, we started telling a much smaller story about a much more powerful technology.

more automation. more agents. more software producing more software. more output from fewer people. more growth. more numbers to prove that something is happening.

and less attention to the person any of this is supposed to be for.

i don’t want to pretend computing had a pure innocent beginning. replacing human labor was one of its ambitions. even in 1960, Licklider distinguished human-computer symbiosis from systems where the remaining people mainly served the machine. he wanted computers to participate in the formation of ideas, not only execute problems already defined.

that distinction feels important – does the system help you discover what you mean? or does it only want you to submit a request, and wait outside while it works?

sometimes waiting is exactly what i want. please do the search. move the files. take away the repetitive work.

but not everything difficult is overhead.

sometimes moving the pieces around is how you understand them. sometimes making the thing changes what you wanted to make. sometimes you need to see the wrong version, touch it, take it apart, and discover a better question.

i want tools that leave room for that relationship.

in his 1981 paper on Smalltalk, Ingalls described a system meant to support everyone’s creative spirit. personal mastery mattered: an individual should be able to comprehend the system, rather than remain dependent on something permanently beyond their reach.

he also argued that computer models should fit the human mind, rather than demand the reverse.

not one perfect workflow for everyone. systems that different people can inhabit differently. someone who thinks through pictures. someone who needs to write. someone who understands a problem by building a simulation. someone whose way of organizing their life doesn’t resemble a SaaS dashboard.

a system you can reshape as your understanding changes.

this is what i want AI to make possible. not just pumping out software, but having a living relationship with it. being able to ask why something works this way. change one part without surrendering the rest. see what happened. undo it. learn enough to make the next change yourself.

the machine can become more capable without making the person smaller.

but that won’t happen just because we make the models better. we have to care about it. design for it. notice when we are making someone more dependent while calling it empowerment.

i don’t want to measure the future only by how much work happens without us.

i want to know what becomes possible for the person who couldn’t participate before.

what can they understand now? what can they express? what can they change without asking permission?

when i say augmenting human intellect, that is what i mean.

not a world that no longer needs us.
a world we have more ability to shape.
tweets.summary_en: Computing should expand people’s ability to think, explore, and solve problems through their relationship with tools. The current emphasis on automation, agents, and output risks sidelining the human capabilities and experiences those tools should serve.

builders.summary_en: An investor letter shares lessons from a decade of evaluating early-stage talent. The visible excerpt introduces the importance of founders but does not show the letter's specific conclusions.
builders.summary_zh: 一封投资人信总结十年来识别早期创业人才的经验。可见片段提到创始人的重要性，但没有展示具体结论。

slang.definition_en: Limited partner, an investor in a venture capital fund.
slang.definition_zh: 有限合伙人，即向风险投资基金出资的投资者。

keywords.definition_zh: 指投资机构写给有限合伙人等基金出资人的信。
keywords.example_zh: 作者分享了一封给基金出资人的信，内容是过去十年投资中识别人才的经验。

keywords.definition_zh: 指识别具有突出能力或发展潜力的人。
keywords.example_zh: 这是该投资人信件的主题，强调从多年投资经历中总结如何发现有潜力的创业人才。

keywords.definition_zh: 指在公司发展初期进行的投资。
keywords.example_zh: 作者引出早期投资重视创始人的常见说法，但可见文字没有展示信中的具体结论。

tweets.text:
This is a LP letter that we recently wrote with our lessons on spotting talent from a decade of investing at the frontier.

https://t.co/v1TnHjvAox

The most common thing you hear about early stage investing is that "It is 90% about the founder".

We agree but have always been unsatisfied by the lack of falsifiability, specificity, and repeatability of that statement.

What are the dimensions of excellence? How do they translate into companies?

It was a pleasure to collaborate with @gopalkraman on this.
tweets.summary_en: A new investor letter distills a decade of lessons on identifying talent, seeking to make founder evaluation more specific, falsifiable, and repeatable. It asks which dimensions of founder excellence matter and how they translate into companies.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary_en: Claude for Legal now offers ready-made workflows for contract review, tracking regulatory changes, and checking citations. Users can add their own documents and connectors, then share the resulting artifacts across their organization.
builders.summary_zh: Claude for Legal 推出预制工作模板，可用于审查合同、追踪监管变化和核查引文。用户可加入自己的文档与连接器，并在组织内分享生成的成果。

slang.definition_en: A shareable output created with an AI tool.
slang.definition_zh: 使用 AI 工具创建、可供分享的成果。

slang.definition_en: An integration that lets software access another data source or service.
slang.definition_zh: 让软件访问其他数据源或服务的集成组件。

keywords.definition_zh: 在 Claude 产品语境中指可独立展示、使用或分享的生成成果。
keywords.example_zh: Claude for Legal 提供现成成果示例，用户可以加入自己的文档和连接器后，在组织内分享。

keywords.definition_zh: 指持续识别和追踪可能影响业务的新兴监管变化。
keywords.example_zh: 这是法律功能库中的一种用途，帮助法律团队提前关注监管动向。

keywords.definition_zh: 指核查法律引用的准确性及其是否支持相关论述。
keywords.example_zh: 它与合同审查等任务并列，表示用户可以从现成示例开始开展法律引文核查。

tweets.text: Learn more: https://t.co/m3tOri9JR3

New in Claude for Legal: a gallery of ready-made artifacts for contract review, regulatory horizon scans, cite checks, and more.

Start from the built-in example, add your own documents and connectors, and share it with anyone across the business. https://t.co/Wn2VK2HeMU

podcasts.name: AI & I by Every
podcasts.title: Can You Use AI To Make Good Art? — With Fred Graver
podcasts.summary_en: The visible transcript argues that AI may help writers and producers facing fewer opportunities understand their strengths, adapt, and create work that supports their careers. The excerpt ends before the argument is developed.
podcasts.summary_zh: 可见逐字稿认为，面对机会减少，写作者和制作人或可借助 AI 认识自身优势、适应变化，并创作有助于职业发展的作品。片段在论述展开前就结束了。

vocab.definition_en: The most advanced limit of development or knowledge in a field.
vocab.definition_zh: 某个领域发展的最前沿；知识或技术的边界。
vocab.example_en: Several labs are competing at the frontier of artificial intelligence.
vocab.example_zh: 多家实验室正在人工智能最前沿展开竞争。

vocab.definition_en: Natural variation in how human brains work; used metaphorically in the sample for differences among AI models.
vocab.definition_zh: 神经多样性，指人类大脑运作方式的自然差异；原文借此比喻不同 AI 模型的差异。
vocab.example_en: The speaker used neurodiversity as a metaphor for the different strengths of AI models.
vocab.example_zh: 演讲者用神经多样性来比喻不同 AI 模型各有所长。

vocab.definition_en: An example that shows a general claim is not always true.
vocab.definition_zh: 反例，用来说明某个普遍性论断并非总是成立的例子。
vocab.example_en: One successful small team can provide a counterexample to the claim that only large organizations innovate.
vocab.example_zh: 一个成功的小团队就能为「只有大型组织才能创新」这一说法提供反例。

vocab.definition_en: A small trial used to evaluate an idea before introducing it more widely.
vocab.definition_zh: 试点；在大范围推广之前，用于评估某个方案的小规模试验。
vocab.example_en: The agency ran a four-week pilot before deciding whether to expand access.
vocab.example_zh: 该机构先开展了为期四周的试点，再决定是否扩大使用范围。

vocab.definition_en: To significantly change how an industry or activity operates, often by introducing new technology.
vocab.definition_zh: 颠覆；通常通过引入新技术，大幅改变一个行业或活动的运作方式。
vocab.example_en: AI could disrupt routine office work while creating demand for new skills.
vocab.example_zh: AI 可能颠覆常规办公室工作，同时创造对新技能的需求。

vocab.definition_en: A period of renewed interest, growth, or activity.
vocab.definition_zh: 复兴；重新受到关注、恢复增长或变得活跃的时期。
vocab.example_en: Handmade goods may enjoy a renaissance as digital products become more common.
vocab.example_zh: 随着数字产品日益普及，手工制品可能迎来复兴。

vocab.definition_en: A small decorative object, usually of little monetary value.
vocab.definition_zh: 小饰物；通常价格不高、用于装饰的小物件。
vocab.example_en: She sells handmade trinkets at the local market.
vocab.example_zh: 她在当地集市出售手工小饰物。

quote.text_en: Well done is better than well said.
quote.author: Benjamin Franklin

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI system that can take actions and use tools to pursue a goal.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 智能体：能够采取行动、使用工具来完成目标的 AI 系统。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Creating an application by describing the desired behavior to an AI in natural language.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 通过自然语言描述需求，让 AI 生成应用的开发方式。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Directing requests or users toward selected models, servers, or destinations.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 流量调度：将请求或用户引导到指定模型、服务器或目标。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Running a trained AI model to produce outputs from inputs.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 推理：运行训练完成的 AI 模型，根据输入生成输出。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A unit of text or other data processed by an AI model.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 词元：AI 模型处理文本或其他数据时使用的基本单位。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI model near the leading edge of current capabilities.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 前沿模型：能力接近当前技术最高水平的 AI 模型。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An especially attractive offer or business opportunity.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 特别划算的优惠，或很有吸引力的商业机会。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Context-dependent shorthand for early startup funding or an initial value controlling randomness.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 依语境可指创业公司的种子轮融资，也可指控制随机过程的初始值；给定片段无法确定具体含义。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Context-dependent shorthand, sometimes referring to a Series A funding round; the excerpt does not establish its meaning.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 依语境而定的简称，有时指 A 轮融资；给定片段无法确定具体含义。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Command-line interface: a way to operate software by typing commands.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 命令行界面：通过输入命令操作软件的方式。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An abbreviation that can mean limited partner in investing or landing page in marketing.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 缩写，投资领域常指有限合伙人，营销领域常指落地页；给定片段无法确定具体含义。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A concrete output of a software or AI workflow, such as a document, code file, or interactive page.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 软件或 AI 工作流程产生的具体成果，例如文档、代码文件或交互页面。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An integration that lets software access another service or data source.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 连接器：让软件访问其他服务或数据源的集成组件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A benchmark or ranking label mentioned in the tweet; its full name and methodology are not provided.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 推文提到的基准测试或排名标签；片段没有提供其全称或评测方法。

slang_glossary.definition_en: To succeed at something difficult or uncertain.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 成功办成一件困难或结果不确定的事。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal phrase for a period when someone or something becomes successful or admired again.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 口语表达，指重新取得成功或重新获得认可的时期，可理解为「强势回归期」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Google DeepMind.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: Google DeepMind 的缩写。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal metaphor for differences in AI models' behavior, strengths, or styles.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 一种非正式比喻，指不同 AI 模型在行为、优势或风格上的差异。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Research organizations developing AI systems near the leading edge of capability.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 研发能力处于技术前沿的 AI 系统的研究机构。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An event or community abbreviation used in the sample; its expansion is not supplied.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 片段中的活动或社区简称；原文未提供全称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Rich Sutton's argument that general methods using computation tend to outperform approaches built around human knowledge over time.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 理查德·萨顿提出的观点：长期来看，利用计算能力的通用方法往往胜过依赖人类知识设计的方法。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An introductory psychology course; used rhetorically to suggest that a point is basic knowledge.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 心理学入门课；此处带有修辞意味，暗示某个道理属于基础常识。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Shorthand for a factor of two; the wording '2x more' can be imprecise.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 两倍的简写；「2x more」这种表达可能存在倍数歧义。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Recorded exercise data before it has been interpreted or turned into recommendations.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 尚未经过解读或转化为建议的原始运动记录。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Informal impressions or sentiment within an organization, rather than measured evaluation results.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 组织内部的主观感受或整体情绪，并非量化评测结果。

slang_glossary.definition_en: To release a product or feature, often gradually to different groups.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 推出或逐步开放产品、功能。

slang_glossary.definition_en: People or teams protecting computer systems and networks against attacks.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 保护计算机系统和网络免受攻击的人员或团队。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In this software context, a configured setup in which the tools can actually run.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在此软件语境中，指已经配置好、工具能够正常运行的环境。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A limited trial before a wider deployment.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 正式大范围部署之前的小规模试点。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A product-specific name for a personal AI companion in the sample.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 片段中对个人 AI 助手的产品专用称呼。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Informal language meaning surprising, extreme, remarkable, or unconventional.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 口语表达，可指惊人的、夸张的、出乎意料的或脑洞大开的。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Three million views; M means million, and views do not necessarily represent unique people.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 三百万次浏览；M 代表百万，浏览次数不一定等于独立浏览人数。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In technology and business, to substantially change an industry's existing practices or economics.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 科技和商业语境中指大幅改变行业现有运作方式或经济模式，常译为「颠覆」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An emphatic way to say that a prediction will prove correct.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 强调自己的预测将会应验，相当于「记住我的话」或「走着瞧」。
